title: Jacket potatoes with roast cauliflower and chickpeas

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain staple; tinned chickpeas, Greek yoghurt and tahini are all acceptable.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including tahini, is an everyday Tesco purchase at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only an oven, a roasting tray, a grater, a knife and a bowl, and the techniques are beginner-level.

works.reason: Potatoes baked for an hour at 200°C with cauliflower and chickpeas roasted for the last 30 minutes will be cooked through, and the quantities suit four.

honest_times.reason: Florets, shredding a quarter cabbage, grating an apple and mixing the dressing fit 15 active minutes, and the 60 cook minutes match the potato bake.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon and the smoked paprika (called paprika in the step), is used, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot jacket potato with spiced roast cauliflower as the main topping suits a mid-January lunch, and the cauliflower is the point of it.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Potato, cauliflower, chickpeas, slaw and yoghurt make a filling, balanced meal a family would happily eat again.
